chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked him about the Name — what is it? He said: 'An attribute of the described.'

key_terms.الِاسْمِ: Al-Ism — 'the Name'; in theological context, refers to the divine names (asma' Allah) used to describe God
key_terms.صِفَةٌ: Sifah — 'attribute' or 'characteristic'; a quality that describes something but is not identical to the thing itself
key_terms.لِمَوْصُوفٍ: Li-mawsuf — 'for/of the described'; the entity being characterized or named; here indicating that names point beyond themselves to the named reality

ai.seo_question: What is a Name according to Imam al-Ridha in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This succinct hadith from Imam al-Ridha (AS) addresses the ontological relationship between divine names (asma') and the named reality. The Imam's answer — that a name is an 'attribute of the described' (sifat li-mawsuf) — establishes a key principle of Shia theology: divine names do not independently exist, but are descriptive attributes pointing to the named entity. This teaching, within the chapter on the 'occurrence of names,' was likely directed at sophisticated students of theology (kalam) who were wrestling with whether God's names are identical with His essence or separate from it.
